title: peatfire-eval: PeatFireBench and evaluation-protocol experiments for district-month fire severity forecasting in Indonesia
description:
PeatFireBench: a district-month benchmark for fire forecasting in Indonesia (498 districts and cities, 2012-2025), built from VIIRS S-NPP active fire detections with the national peat map (Ministry of Agriculture 2019, via Trase), GFWED fire weather, ENSO and IOD indices, CHIRPS rainfall, land cover, forest loss, terrain and population; twelve baselines; chronological, extreme-year and island-transfer splits; two severity targets. The raw panel and covariate tables are included; the feature panel is rebuilt by the scripts. Accompanies the manuscript Evaluation choices change which fire forecasting model a district would choose: PeatFireBench, a 498-district benchmark for Indonesia.

Version 2.1.1 adds the analyses of the third review round: district-relative FWI baselines, five further seeds with a seed-averaged provincial ranking, per-year calibration with intervals, a provincial check of the peat crosswalk, and results split by peat and non-peat districts.

Version 2.2.0 adds the West Kalimantan ranking-stability analyses (year-clustered bootstrap with exact enumeration, record-length projection, discarding non-fire test months, seed sensitivity) for the manuscript How Stable Are Fire Prediction Model Rankings? Bootstrap Evidence From West Kalimantan, with their logs.

Version 2.3.0 adds, for PeatFireBench, the decision value of the warnings (hit rate and false alarm ratio of a fixed alert rule, relative economic value over cost-loss ratios) and the components of the Fire Weather Index System (Drought Code, Duff Moisture Code, Fine Fuel Moisture Code, Buildup Index) taken from the monthly GFWED v2.0 files, with their logs.

Version 2.4.0 adds the revision analyses for PeatFireBench: the scripts of five registered analysis rounds (phases A-E) comparing every model with reference climatologies computed from training years on the same rows (EF-1m, EF-3m), a probability climatology chosen on training years (EF-P) and the calendar adjusted with last month's national detections (EF-L), with year-level intervals, equivalence tests, proper scores, alert rules, provinces and peat strata; the design and results records (registration/, Indonesian) and logs.

Version 2.5.0 adds the sixth registered round (phase F): EF-L scored as a ranking (within-year AUC-PR) and under six alert rules, including a monthly quota whose share is tuned on training years, gradient boosting refitted with the national detection anomaly, and extreme-year Brier skill over EF-L with district intervals; with its design and results record and logs.

Version 2.6.0 adds the seventh registered round (phase G): the minimum detectable Brier skill over EF-L, probability scores with thresholds from training years, and a test of EF-L on the MODIS years 2003-2011 (MODIS_SP Collection 6/6.1, same filter and district polygons; download, confidence-class and evaluation scripts), with its design and results record and logs. In the revised manuscript the benchmark is named IndoFireBench.

Version 2.7.0 adds the eighth registered round (phase H): the MODIS test repeated with training only on years before 2016 and with thresholds from training years, the training-selected probability climatology (EF-P), the level-shift diagnostic and Brier skill as one ratio on MODIS, with its design and results record and logs.

Version 2.8.0 adds rounds nine to twelve (phases I-L): six gradient-boosting seeds and a training-length control on MODIS, the level-shift diagnostic split into a period offset and the year-to-year level, the minimum detectable difference, the only MODIS forecast (test years 2008-2019, each trained on earlier years only), cross-validation with a one-year buffer, peat districts on VIIRS, and the forward forecast and the VIIRS probability results averaged over years in three ways (mean of yearly ratios, one ratio over all test rows, median year), with their design and results records, logs and the main-results figure script.

Version 2.9.0 adds the thirteenth round (phase M): two drought forms of the level-adjusted calendar on VIIRS (EF-D with the district's previous-month Drought Code in place of the national detection count, EF-LD with both), bootstrap Monte Carlo error (five seeds, 10,000 draws) and a moving-block year bootstrap for the forward MODIS forecast, and the ENSO and dipole phase of every test year, with its design and results record and logs.

Version 2.10.0 adds the fourteenth round (phase N): the drought forms EF-D and EF-LD scored on the forward MODIS forecast, with the GFWED Drought Code of December 2002 to December 2011 aggregated to districts (new table), the level-shift share of the forward forecast split into a period offset and the level of each year, and sign and signed-rank tests over the forward years for both targets, with its design and results record and logs.

Version 2.11.0 adds the fifteenth round (phase O): gradient boosting refitted on the forward MODIS forecast with the district Drought Code anomaly used by EF-LD and scored over the four references, with bootstrap Monte Carlo error and a moving-block year bootstrap; the main-results figure script with that series; the registered protocol for evaluating the 2026 season with its two dated addenda (registration/Hasil_Patokan_21.md, registered before standard-processing 2026 data were released); and the commit history of every registration record. The revised manuscript is now titled IndoFireBench: a district benchmark and reference forecasts for monthly fire forecasting in Indonesia.

Version 2.11.1 adds the VIIRS part of phase O, left out of 2.11.0: gradient boosting given the district Drought Code anomaly on the chronological test years 2020-2025, scored over EF-LD, EF-L, the raw calendar and EF-P (patokan_tingkat_o.py), with its logs.

Version 2.11.2 adds the sixteenth round (phase P): the fire-level share of gradient boosting's probability gain over the raw calendar on the chronological test years 2020-2025, recomputed with thresholds, evaluated districts and calendars from the training years of each fold (patokan_tingkat_p.py), with its design and results record and logs; Figure 3 labels the MODIS model GB-FH. The revised manuscript is now titled IndoFireBench: a district benchmark with reference forecasts for monthly fire prediction in Indonesia.

Version 2.11.4 adds the eighteenth round (phase R): the gradient boosting model's own level error beside the calendar's in the relation of phase Q, and two-stage intervals with provinces instead of districts resampled for every full-panel cell of the VIIRS probability table (patokan_tingkat_r1.py, patokan_tingkat_r.py, patokan_modis_r.py), with its design and results record and logs, and a fourth dated addendum to the 2026 protocol: a prediction of the fire level taken from the 2026 per-district gain given the calendar's level error, with coefficients fixed from the existing years (patokan_ramalan_2026.py).

Version 2.11.3 adds the seventeenth round (phase Q): the fire level removed from each test year related to the calendar's level error that year, and two-stage intervals with provinces instead of districts resampled (patokan_tingkat_q.py, patokan_modis_q.py), with its design and results record and logs, and a third dated addendum to the 2026 protocol that moves the 2027 registration to before 1 January 2027.

Versions 1.0.0-1.3.0 hold earlier analyses of West Kalimantan and of the five Kalimantan provinces, kept unchanged because they are cited. Version 1.3.0 corrected the ONI timing (each three-month season assigned to its last month).
